source: Hernandez, Schmidt, Okudan Kremer (2012) Experimental assessment of TRIZ effectiveness in idea generation
finding: Multi-site experiment (UTEP, Penn State, Maryland). TRIZ taught by one lecture plus handouts raised novelty and variety but cut idea quantity compared with control groups.
numbers: Task: traffic light redesign, function 'counter snow'. UTEP: 21 control, 9 TRIZ. Maryland: 20 control, 21 TRIZ. Penn State 4 sections of 120 students. Novelty ANOVA p values listed as 0.0004, 0.0145, 0.5786 (one per site, table garbled in PDF, so site order uncertain). Quantity p values 0.2879, 0.5409, 0.6291 (all not significant). One Penn State quantity cell reads 16.286 vs 4.100, which looks like a team vs individual unit difference.
quote: TRIZ improves some of the metrics while worsening others.
limits: Authors admit some results are below p=0.05 and call them a trend. Training was one lecture. TRIZ group had a first no-method session before training. Only 1 design task. Table text garbled so per-site numbers are uncertain.
agent_relevance: A short TRIZ prompt trades idea count for novelty. For an agent, test novelty per token, not raw count.

source: Hernandez, Schmidt, Okudan Kremer (2012) Experimental assessment of TRIZ effectiveness in idea generation
finding: Background section reports earlier TRIZ and analogy studies used to frame the experiment (Okudan et al. brainstorming vs TRIZ plus brainstorming; Howard et al. UK industry; Chan et al. analogy distance).
numbers: Okudan et al.: TRIZ plus brainstorming gave better novelty, variety and quality on a fume hood task. Chan et al.: 153 senior engineering students; analogies from far domains raised novelty but lowered idea count. Howard et al.: TRIZ principles helped designers find less obvious ideas in brainstorming.
limits: Secondhand summaries inside the paper. I did not open Okudan, Howard or Chan.
agent_relevance: Far-domain stimulus gives novelty but costs quantity. That matches what TRIZ principles do. Gate the reframe operator so it fires after a plain draft exists.

source: Ogot and Okudan (2006) Integrating systematic creativity into first-year engineering design curriculum
finding: First-year course at Penn State. Sections that learned the TRIZ contradiction matrix produced about twice as many feasible concepts per team on a common industry fume hood problem.
numbers: TRIZ: 16 teams (64 students, 2 sections). Non-TRIZ: 24 teams (96 students, 3 sections picked from 12). Feasible concepts per team 8.94 vs 4.42. Unique solutions per section 35 vs 16.3. Unique concepts no other group had: 21 vs 8. Section means: TRIZ 8.38 and 9.50; non-TRIZ 4.88, 3.75, 4.63.
quote: TRIZ makes it easier for students to generate feasible concepts.
limits: Quasi-experiment, whole sections, no random assignment, no stated significance test, quantity only (no novelty or quality score). Instructors observed students drifting off the principles without monitoring.
agent_relevance: The gain came with guided practice and monitoring. A scaffold that checks the principle is actually applied matters.

source: Cano-Moreno et al. (2022) Using TRIZ10 for enhancing creativity in engineering design education
finding: Simplified TRIZ (TRIZ10, ten principles, 30 minute lecture) in a small proof-of-concept study: ideas roughly doubled and mean novelty rose about 10 percent.
numbers: N=13 students in 3 groups. Average added ideas from TRIZ10 178 percent. Mean novelty 3.6 for own ideas, 3.9 and 4.1 in the other sessions; per-group novelty gain 18.6, 4.3, 6.2, 9.7 percent as read from the table. Learning efficiency 75 percent overall.
limits: N=13, no control group, sessions are sequential so order and warm-up effects are mixed in. Table text is garbled in places.
agent_relevance: Shows a reduced principle set may be enough. Supports a small typed reframe set rather than all 40 principles.

source: Cano-Moreno et al. (2022) Using TRIZ10 for enhancing creativity in engineering design education
finding: Table 1 in the paper lists earlier TRIZ teaching studies with mixed outcomes by metric.
numbers: Dumas 2016 (N=44): fluency down 19.3 percent after 50 min TRIZ lecture. Chang 2016 (N=121, 60 control, 61 TRIZ): originality up 1.5 percent. Dumas and Schmidt 2015 (N=19): 6 week course, novelty up 30.8 percent, creative products up 21.7 percent, resolution up 15.9 percent, no difference in elaboration. A further study in the table: novelty up 48.8 percent, ideas down 12.5 percent.
limits: Secondhand table, units and baselines differ per study. I did not open the original papers. Row alignment in the PDF text is partly garbled.
agent_relevance: Pattern across studies: novelty up, fluency flat or down. Matches the 2012 multi-site result.

source: ICDC 2012 Design cognition differences when using structured and unstructured concept generation creativity techniques
finding: Protocol study: when students used TRIZ they spent more of their reasoning on the problem (function and expected behaviour) than when brainstorming. The gap faded by the second half of the session.
numbers: 11 teams of 2 mechanical engineering seniors (22 students), same two tasks, one with brainstorming and one with TRIZ, FBS coding. Issue index brainstorming mean 0.177 (SD 0.069) in one half; paired t tests significant for the full session (p<0.005 and p<0.001 reported); second half process index t(9)=-0.195, p>0.05.
limits: Small N, preliminary, no outcome quality measure, task and technique order not confirmed as counterbalanced.
agent_relevance: TRIZ works partly by forcing problem-space time early. An agent step for problem reframing should run early, not late.

source: Frillici, Rotini, Fiorineschi (2016) Re-design the design task through TRIZ tools
finding: Group's own task-clarification proposal: TRIZ Functional Modelling plus System Operator (nine screens) used to question the task in the requirement list before FDM begins. Single industrial case, no controlled test.
numbers: One case: concrete slab plant. Firm asked for a conveyor belt to recover fallen mix; analysis moved the task to a new dispenser that avoids leakage. Functional model: drawer had 2 of 3 functions insufficient.
quote: the right problem may not be the one stated
limits: One case, no control, no counts of ideas, authors are the method developers. No measure given.
agent_relevance: Direct precedent for a typed reframe operator (O4/O8 style). The only evidence is a single narrative case.

source: Frillici, Rotini, Fiorineschi (2016) Re-design the design task through TRIZ tools
finding: Paper states why FDM creativity support is thin: abstraction broadens the problem but does not find the real crux, and psychological inertia anchors the task.
numbers: Prior integrations of TRIZ with Pahl and Beitz cited: Malmqvist 1996, Dietz 2009, Nix 2011, Frillici 2014, Cascini 2011.
limits: Argument by the authors, not measured.
agent_relevance: Names the exact gap our row is about. Evidence of the gap itself is argument, not data.

source: Fiorineschi, Frillici, Rotini (2019) Teaching and learning design methods: facing the related issues with TRIZ
finding: Same group applies TRIZ problem-solving tools to the teaching of their FDM-style conceptual design course. Output is a set of suggestions, not a measured improvement.
numbers: Course: Mechanical Engineering, Florence, 12 of about 30 conceptual design hours, 5 hours lectures, teams of 2 to 3. Evidence is student questionnaires from past editions. Students see the advantages but abandon methods later.
limits: No pre-post measure, no control group, no outcome numbers. Authors say future editions could be compared.
agent_relevance: Reminder that adoption fails when perceived effort is high. A scaffold must stay cheap per step.

source: Chen et al. (2024) TRIZ-GPT: an LLM-augmented method for problem-solving
finding: GPT-4 given a TRIZ workflow (problem to contradiction to principle to solution). Contradiction recall depended on prompt style; few-shot hurt recall.
numbers: Case set A: 37 classic cases (34 tested after 3 used for few-shot). Recall: basic 0.675, chain-of-thought 0.691, few-shot 0.245, CoT plus few-shot 0.247. Precision 0.259, 0.310, 0.333, 0.298. At least one gold contradiction found in 85.3 percent (basic) and 88.2 percent (CoT) of cases.
limits: Gold is one textbook contradiction per case; precision low because the model lists many parameters. Classic cases may be in training data (hence set B).
agent_relevance: Plain chain of thought beats few-shot for finding contradictions. Few-shot may anchor on the example count.

source: Chen et al. (2024) TRIZ-GPT: an LLM-augmented method for problem-solving
finding: Solution step: cosine similarity between GPT-4 solutions and the documented solutions did not differ across four prompt strategies. GPT-4 beat GPT-3.5 on post-cutoff cases.
numbers: 84 principle-case pairs, embedding cosine similarity about 0.82 (basic M=0.829, SD 0.031; CoT 0.823; few-shot 0.824; CoT plus few-shot 0.824), no significant difference. Set B: 10 cases published after April 2023 used for GPT-4 vs GPT-3.5; GPT-4 had higher recall.
limits: Embedding similarity to a known solution measures resemblance to the textbook answer, not novelty or feasibility. No human rating. No no-TRIZ baseline.
agent_relevance: Prompt wording at the solution step did not matter much; the principle choice step did. No evidence here that TRIZ structure beats free LLM ideation.

source: Jiang and Luo (2025 preprint) AutoTRIZ: automating engineering innovation with TRIZ and LLMs
finding: AutoTRIZ fixes the TRIZ steps as code and uses GPT-4 inside. On 10 textbook cases it matched textbook contradiction analysis in the top 3 on 7.
numbers: 100 runs per case, entropy 0 to 6.64. 7 of 10 cases complete or half match within top 3 detections. Cases 5,6,7,8 had one dominant answer. In most cases one parameter was stable and the other varied. Higher-probability outputs matched better.
limits: Only 10 cases, textbook answer is not ground truth (authors say so), one expert co-author checked the battery case. No comparison against plain LLM ideation with scores.
agent_relevance: Self-consistency across samples gives a confidence signal: agreement predicts match with experts. Usable as a gate.

source: Jiang and Luo (2025 preprint) AutoTRIZ: automating engineering innovation with TRIZ and LLMs
finding: Battery thermal management case study: TRIZ-structured LLM design compared with the best existing scheme on three engineering metrics.
numbers: Improvements reported +24 percent, +64 percent, +26 percent over the best existing scheme. One case.
limits: One case, author-run, no blind rating, no baseline LLM without TRIZ in the numbers. The authors also say vanilla ChatGPT needs more detailed input.
agent_relevance: Case result only. Not evidence that the TRIZ steps cause the gain.

source: Mohammadi and Zeng (2025) Enhancing TRIZ through environment-based design methodology supported by a large language model
finding: TRIZ plus environment-based design with an LLM (GPT-3.5) generated more ideas and higher variety than TRIZ experts on 3 textbook problems, but idea quality varied widely and functional analysis accuracy was about 50 percent.
numbers: Quantity LLM vs expert: case 1 20 vs 4, case 2 7 vs 2, case 3 18 vs 1 or 2. Novelty means (two evaluators) case 1 2.42/3.41 vs 2.0/2.56; case 2 2.13/1.49 vs 1.77/2.07; case 3 2.79/3.32 vs 1.43/2.57. Question generation correctness 0.82 to 0.91, interaction extraction correctness 0.82 to 0.87.
limits: 3 cases, 2 evaluators, expert baseline had 1 to 4 ideas so quantity comparison is unfair. In case 2 evaluator 2 rated the experts higher on novelty. LLM did not always follow prompt rules (treated 'is' as an action verb).
agent_relevance: LLM is cheap on volume; the value test is quality after filtering. Needs a judge step that rejects ideas that fail the contradiction.

source: Wang and Uzzi (2026) Inventive problem solving with LLMs: a benchmark for TRIZ reasoning (TRIZBench)
finding: TRIZBench: large patent-grounded benchmark. LLMs detect that a contradiction exists far better than they name the right parameter pair.
numbers: Case-level contradiction detection F1 about 0.75 to 0.87 for zero-shot and few-shot Qwen3, LLaMA3.1, Gemini-2.5-Pro; pair F1 only 0.29 to 0.42; patent pair Hit@3 0.13 to 0.28 (LoRA best 0.28, PatentSBERTa retrieval 0.23 to 0.26). Dataset: 590 source documents, 734 cases with principles (54.2 percent).
limits: Labels produced partly by Gemini-2.5-pro plus human check (74 percent agreement before adjudication). Only the tables I could extract were read.
agent_relevance: LLMs see the conflict but misname it. A reframe step needs retrieval or checking, not pure prompting.

source: Wang and Uzzi (2026) Inventive problem solving with LLMs: a benchmark for TRIZ reasoning (TRIZBench)
finding: Principle prediction improves with TRIZ structure and retrieval; direct prompting underperforms.
numbers: Principle Hit@3 with a small set: 0.67 on cases, 0.48 on patents for retrieval. Best reranking pipelines Hit@3 up to 0.71 on cases and 0.59 on patents (Qwen3-8B M-Rerank). Direct zero-shot Qwen3-8B Hit@3 0.39 (cases) and 0.27 (patents).
limits: Metric is match to source-linked principles, not usefulness of the resulting idea. Several principles can fit one problem.
agent_relevance: Structured retrieval of principles roughly doubles hit rate over free prompting on this benchmark.

source: Fiorineschi, Frillici, Rotini (2018) Supporting systematic conceptual design with TRIZ
finding: Key paper. Says most systematic conceptual design methods rest on functional decomposition and morphology (FDM), that FDM gives weak creativity support, and that earlier TRIZ-FDM merges had issues. Proposes another way and demonstrates it on three academic examples.
numbers: No effect sizes. Three academic demonstrations. DOI 10.21278/idc.2018.0135.
limits: Seen only through the abstract in a search result. Full text needs sign-in.
agent_relevance: The paper itself offers no controlled test, so the claim that FDM is non-comprehensive for creativity is argument.

source: Frillici, Fiorineschi, Cascini (2015) Linking TRIZ to conceptual design engineering approaches
finding: Compares Pahl and Beitz systematic approach with TRIZ. Notes Malmqvist et al. gave merging tips but no case study.
numbers: No numbers.
limits: Download returned HTML, only a search snippet seen.
agent_relevance: Confirms the TRIZ-with-systematic-design literature starts with proposals, not measurements.

source: Valentine, Belski, Hamilton (2017) Can idea generation techniques impede effective ideation
finding: Failed replication of the Belski group earlier gains from a simple ideation technique. No differences between control and technique groups.
numbers: Mean distinct ideas 5.03 (control), 5.04 (pen and paper), 4.20 (computer). No significant differences between groups.
limits: Search snippet only; technique was a simple TRIZ-derived ideation method, not full TRIZ. Fetch of the PDF failed.
agent_relevance: Gains from structured prompts are not stable across cohorts. Treat a single positive result with caution.

source: Belski, Hourani, Valentine et al. (2014) Simple ideation: enhancing idea generation
finding: RMIT students: a Su-Field-based prompt group produced significantly more ideas than the other groups (Kruskal-Wallis). Control averaged 2 dissimilar ideas.
numbers: Control group 16 minutes silent ideation, about 2 dissimilar ideas each. Exact p not seen.
limits: Snippet only. Positive result later not replicated in 2017.
agent_relevance: Same group has one positive and one null result.

source: Belski et al. (2015) Simple ideation influencing idea generation
finding: Follow-up with other year levels reported a statistically significant gain in independent solution ideas vs control.
numbers: Exact figures not seen.
limits: Snippet only. Same authors as the original, not independent.
agent_relevance: Replication by the originators; independent replications are missing.

source: Spreafico and Russo (2016) TRIZ industrial case studies: a critical survey
finding: Survey of over 200 industrial TRIZ case studies from TRIZ Journal and ETRIA conference. Most used tools are the contradiction matrix and 40 principles. Spread of TRIZ has not reached the expected level.
numbers: Over 200 cases. Sector shares energy and electrical 19 percent, home appliances 14 percent, generic mechanical 14 percent.
limits: Seen via search summary only; cases are self-selected successes, not controlled.
agent_relevance: Industrial evidence is publication-selected. No failure cases are collected.

source: Design Science (2020) neuro-cognitive comparison of brainstorming, morphological analysis and TRIZ
finding: 30 engineering students: brainstorming and morphological analysis needed more prefrontal activation than TRIZ.
numbers: N=30. Effect sizes not seen.
limits: Search snippet only.
agent_relevance: TRIZ may lower cognitive load per step. Suggests structured prompts reduce search effort.

source: Livotov group modified TRIZ principles study (via search summary)
finding: Less abstract wording of modified sub-principles gave more ideas than classical principles.
numbers: About 1.5 times more ideas reported in the summary.
limits: Snippet only, exact source and year uncertain, treat as unverified.
agent_relevance: Wording of the principle matters: concrete phrasing beats abstract phrasing.

source: Comparison of ideation techniques for beginning designers (102 first-year students)
finding: Design heuristics, morphological analysis and individual brainstorming compared; brainstorming gave the most concepts in a 25 minute session.
numbers: N=102 first-year students, 25 minute session.
limits: Snippet only, no TRIZ arm, year uncertain.
agent_relevance: Under tight time, plain brainstorming wins on count. Structure costs time.
